name: Nebius ConTree (Token Factory Sandboxes)

modes.label: Sandboxes beta (free, per-command microVM executions)
modes.note: Rates null on purpose: free during beta, no paid rate published, per-execution vCPU/RAM undocumented. Free while in beta ('runs don't consume your credits'); approval required. Each command runs in its own microVM (0.4-2 s startup with cached image) and its filesystem result is snapshotted as an image; compute exists only while a command executes. vCPU/RAM per execution is not selectable or documented, so a 4 vCPU/8 GiB shape is not guaranteed. Post-beta pricing unpublished ('pay per execution, not idle').

plans.name: Sandboxes Beta
plans.note: Nebius Token Factory account + beta approval. 50 simultaneously running operations (raisable on request). max_session_h 1 = per-operation timeout from the API spec example (instance_max_timeout 3600 s), unverified; multi-hour agent sessions are chains of executions resuming from snapshotted images. No personal/sensitive data during beta.

caveats: Product is in BETA and FREE ('runs don't consume your credits'); rates of 0 reflect the beta, not a sustainable price. Post-beta pricing is unpublished; the homepage promises 'pay per execution, not idle' and the API returns a per-operation cost field.

Execution model differs from long-lived sandboxes: each command is its own microVM; the filesystem (not memory/processes) is committed as an immutable image after every non-disposable run, and later commands branch from any image. No services, no inbound network, no SSH.
No vCPU/RAM sizing in the API; the 4 vCPU/8 GiB workload shape cannot be requested. Writable layer default 12 GiB (included_disk_gib).
Beta limits: 50 simultaneously running operations; untagged unreferenced images may be deleted after 180 days; access by application; no personal/sensitive data.
max_session_h 1 is the per-operation timeout from the API spec example (3600 s); real limit unverified.

The API spec's default base URL is now https://api.tokenfactory.nebius.com/sandboxes. Token Factory's own front-end config maps that host to eu-north1 (Finland), so EU is still the inference, and the docs still don't state a region. No region choice for Sandboxes.
Outbound internet: API networking.enabled defaults true but the blog says it 'may depend on deployment configuration'; only on/off control (no allowlist).
Nebius holds SOC 2 Type II / ISO 27001 at company level, but beta terms exclude sensitive data, so compliance flags are left null.
Launched as ConTree early access 2026-02-19 (contree.dev blog); became Nebius Token Factory 'Sandboxes' beta 2026-05-19. SDK/CLI/MCP are Apache-2.0; service is closed.
Free during beta; no paid rate published, so not priced.

Re-checked 2026-09-28: tokenfactory.nebius.com/sandboxes/about and docs.tokenfactory.nebius.com/sandboxes/overview publish no rate (beta; pricing questions go to contree@nebius.com). Kept unpriced: free beta, not a missing number.
The writable layer is configurable per execution (resources_limits.max_layer_bytes, default 12 GiB). CPU and RAM are still not selectable.

A running operation's VM can host extra subprocesses (POST /operations/{id}/subprocesses) with stdin kept open, so one VM can serve several processes until the operation's timeout. The model is still batch-style: no inbound network, and only the filesystem persists.

fleet.notes: Beta docs limit simultaneously running operations to 50; encoded as operation-backed sandbox ceiling, not retained image count. Contact provider to lift beta restrictions; no guaranteed approval time or KYC checklist. API schema example instance_max_concurrency=10 is an example, not used to override published 50.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: ConTree saves an immutable filesystem snapshot after every execution, so agents can fork from any checkpoint, explore multiple paths in parallel, and revert instantly.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: end of every non-disposable execution (each command is its own microVM; the result is committed as a new immutable image, result_image_uuid). Filesystem only: 'Process memory, running services, and network state are not preserved.' Opt out per run with disposable=true.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Fork execution state at any checkpoint. Explore multiple solution paths in parallel, then score results and expand the best branches.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Checkpoints are the per-execution images (you choose when by running a command non-disposably; tags name them). Any image can boot any number of new microVM executions (fork/branch, rollback). Filesystem only, no memory; you cannot checkpoint a VM mid-execution.

harness_api.quote: Integrate your own agent via contree-sdk.
harness_api.note: SDK/CLI/MCP let an external agent run commands and branch images; no first-party API to run or drive a coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) inside the sandbox. 'contree agent' only prints a manual for agents using the CLI.

egress_allowlist.quote: Enable network access for the instance. When `false`, the VM starts without a guest network interface.
egress_allowlist.note: No-internet mode only (networking.enabled, default true). No domain or IP allowlist in the API; level null because it is all-or-nothing.

egress_http_rules.quote: Enable network access for the instance. When `false`, the VM starts without a guest network interface.
egress_http_rules.note: The only network knob in the OpenAPI spec is the enabled boolean; no HTTP-level rules.

ingress_rules.quote: Executions have no inbound network access.
ingress_rules.note: No inbound networking at all (no ports, URLs, SSH), so there is nothing to configure; batch execution model.

guest_firewall.quote: Full root inside the VM, zero access outside it.
guest_firewall.note: Derived: microVM per execution with 'Dedicated kernel, hardware boundary' and full root. Rules only live for one execution (network state is not preserved) and whether the guest kernel ships netfilter modules is undocumented.

secret_proxy.quote: Pass secrets via env, not files
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are plain env vars passed per run / per CLI session (stored in local SQLite by the CLI); no credential-injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Maximum writable layer size in bytes.
volume_attach.note: Storage per execution = image rootfs + writable layer (default 12 GiB, resources_limits.max_layer_bytes) + uploaded files; the OpenAPI spec has no volume object.

volume_shared.quote: Each non-disposable execution produces a new image.
volume_shared.note: No shared/network volumes. Many executions can start from the same immutable image in parallel, but that is copy-on-write branching, not a shared read-write mount.
